Russian Mission|United States of America.f: Began as an 1842 Russian-American Company fur trading post called Ikogmiut, and got its present name in the early 1900s.

Skagway|United States of America.f: The name comes from the Tlingit sha-ka-gei, an idiom for the rough seas that strong north winds whip up in Taiya Inlet.

Rampart|United States of America.f: Novelist Rex Beach prospected here in 1900, and a proposed Rampart Dam would have made the world's largest man-made reservoir.

Nikolski|United States of America.f: Thought to be one of the world's oldest continuously occupied communities, its Chaluka site shows 4,000 years of near-constant use.

King Cove|United States of America.f: A long-disputed road to Cold Bay through Izembek National Wildlife Refuge was proposed for medical flights grounded by weather or darkness.

Chuathbaluk|United States of America.f: The name comes from the Yup'ik Curapalek, meaning the hills where the big blueberries grow.

Elim|United States of America.f: Elim is the westernmost point in the range of black spruce.

Manley Hot Springs|United States of Amer.f: In 1907 miner Frank Manley built a four-storey hot springs hotel here with 45 rooms and an indoor Olympic-size pool.

Hoonah|United States of America.f: Hoonah comes from the Tlingit Xunaa, meaning lee of the north wind, and it is the only first-class city on Chichagof Island.

Ouzinkie|United States of America.f: Saint Herman, America's first canonized Orthodox saint, lived on nearby Spruce Island for over twenty years until his death in 1836.

Mertarvik|United States of America.f: The village was built to take in residents of eroding Newtok, and by 2024 all of Newtok's people had moved there.

Hooper Bay|United States of America.f: A fire on August 3, 2006 destroyed about 15 acres of the town, including 35 structures and all of its schools.

Koliganek|United States of America.f: The present Koliganek is the third village to bear the name along the Nushagak River since the late 19th century.

Perryville|United States of America.f: Founded by refugees of the 1912 Katmai eruption, it was named for K.W. Perry, captain of the revenue cutter that carried them.

Takotna|United States of America.f: The village was founded where the river became too shallow for Arthur Berry's small sternwheeler, and was first called Berry Landing.

Pilot Point|United States of America.f: Pilot Point has depended for its existence on the big seasonal returns of Pacific salmon, especially sockeye.

Napakiak|United States of America.f: Napakiak is the end of a unique 8.5-mile prototype single-wire earth return power line from Bethel, built in 1981.

Montauk|United States of America.f: Montauk claims more world saltwater fishing records than any other port, and its lighthouse from 1792 is New York's oldest.

Eek|United States of America.f: The name comes from a Yupik word meaning two eyes, and it often appears on lists of unusual place names.

Chefornak|United States of America.f: An extinct volcano, Tern Mountain, rises to the south, and large blocky igneous rocks are common around the village.

Chevak|United States of America.f: Chevak people speak Cup'ik rather than Yup'ik, an identity that let them form their own school district.

Buckland|United States of America.f: The town is named for the Buckland River, which was named for Oxford professor William Buckland.

Marshall|United States of America.f: Once called Fortuna Ledge after a mining camp, it took back the name Marshall in 1984, reportedly for Vice President Thomas Marshall.

Nightmute|United States of America.f: Its Yup'ik name Negtemiut literally means the people of the pressed-down place.

Kipnuk|United States of America.f: The name means a bend, after the bend in the Kugkaktlik River where the village sits.

Toksook Bay|United States of America.f: Toksook Bay was founded in 1964 when residents of nearby Nightmute relocated by dogsled to the coast.

Akiak|United States of America.f: Akiak means the other side, because the site was a winter crossing toward the Yukon River basin.

Kwethluk|United States of America.f: Kwethluk is the birthplace of Saint Olga of Alaska.

Kalskag|United States of America.f: Upper and Lower Kalskag are two villages linked by a single two-mile gravel road, and they share one airport.

Akhiok|United States of America.f: Residents of Kaguyak moved to Akhiok after the 1964 earthquake and tsunami destroyed their village.

Anacortes|United States of America.f: The name adapts Anne Curtis Bowman, wife of early Fidalgo Island settler Amos Bowman.
